findings.title: Recorded sample sizes render as blanks
findings.why: The value cell makes the sample sizes appear unavailable, although the trial row records both. The renderer reads n1/n2 instead of nc1/nc2.
findings.fix: Render the recorded continuous-outcome denominators: 137 and 144.

findings.title: Absence label incorrectly denies an outcome sentence
findings.page_quote: not in cached source -- no outcome sentence/effect found

evidence.quote: However, melatonin had no significant effect on other objective sleep parameters including sleep latency, sleep efficiency, wake during the sleep and percent of N1, N3 and REM sleep.

findings.why: The label appears for PMID 33157425, whose recorded source explicitly discusses sleep latency. Missing poolable numerical inputs do not mean no outcome sentence was found.
findings.fix: State that the source mentions the outcome but provides no poolable effect with uncertainty or usable arm-level inputs.

findings.title: Forest plot displays risk ratios on an odds-ratio axis
findings.why: The plot labels its axis OR but displays 1.67 for PMID 19522426, its risk ratio. The recorded trial odds ratio is approximately 2.78. The other count-based trial markers likewise display risk ratios alongside an odds-ratio pooled estimate.
findings.fix: Draw trial markers and labels from the recorded study_effect values on the declared OR scale.

findings.title: Published-rate reconstructions are labeled AACT-derived

evidence.quote: arm counts recovered from the published rate + denominator (percentage round-trip matches the committed abstract)

findings.why: For PMID 19522426 and PMID 16769748, the recorded verification concerns reconstruction from published abstract rates and denominators. It does not establish AACT derivation.
findings.fix: Label these rows as published-rate reconstructions verified against the committed abstract.

findings.title: Forest plot labels a relative-risk trial as HR
findings.why: The forest plot presents PMID 19717844's 0.66 estimate under a single HR axis label without identifying that row as RR. The review explicitly records RR.
findings.fix: Identify each trial's measure and disclose the mixed HR/RR presentation in the forest plot.

findings.title: Composite description contradicts the selected FOURIER endpoint
findings.page_quote: pooled trials use each trial's OWN primary composite

evidence.quote: ClinicalTrials.gov outcome measure #1: Time to Cardiovascular Death, Myocardial Infarction, or Stroke
the key secondary endpoint (composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, and stroke) was tested at a significance level of 0.05.

findings.why: The selected FOURIER result is its three-component secondary endpoint. The page instead describes all pooled inputs as primary composites and describes FOURIER's five-component primary endpoint elsewhere in the same tab.
findings.fix: Describe the selected three-component secondary FOURIER endpoint and reconcile the composite-heterogeneity and definition-audit wording with that selection.
